proof_nl:
Let n>1 and let r be real with (n-1)/n <= r < 1. We show that every floor term in the definition of f_n(r) is determined explicitly.

Fix k with 1 <= k <= n. From r >= (n-1)/n we get kr >= k(n-1)/n. Since k <= n, we have k(n-1)/n >= k-1. Also r < 1 implies kr < k. Therefore
k-1 <= kr < k.
Hence floor(k r) = k-1 for every k=1,2,...,n.

In particular, floor(nr)=n-1, and
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k r)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (k-1)/k = sum_{k=1}^n (1 - 1/k) = n - H_n,
where H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Therefore
f_n(r) = floor(nr) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k r)/k = (n-1) - (n - H_n) = H_n - 1.
This is exactly the desired identity.
solver_summary: For r in [(n-1)/n,1), one has k-1 <= kr < k for every k=1,...,n, so floor(kr)=k-1. Substituting into the definition of f_n gives f_n(r)=H_n-1.
vetter_reason: The proof directly establishes the universal statement: for any real r with (n-1)/n <= r < 1, one has floor(kr)=k-1 for all 1<=k<=n, hence floor(nr)=n-1 and f_n(r)=H_n-1. This matches the lemma exactly, with no gaps or dependency issues.
